speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my care. I see you are a newborn with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; this is a serious symptom that requires us to move quickly. Can you tell me exactly when this vomiting started, and has it been projectile or continuous? Also, has there been any passage of stool, and if so, was it green or black?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray to look for pneumoperitoneum and obstruction. Also, can you confirm if any meconium has passed since birth, or is the abdomen distended?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray Abdomen findings show a 'double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia; no pneumoperitoneum observed; abdomen is distended.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with midgut volvulus. The history of bilious vomiting in a newborn within the first 24 hours, combined with a family history of surgical intervention for pyloric stenosis, strongly suggests an anatomical defect requiring immediate surgical evaluation rather than gastroenteritis. Please confirm the abdominal X-ray results showing dilated loops and a lack of air in the distal bowel, and REQUEST IMAGES to confirm the "double bubble" sign or other signs of obstruction.
